rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise means Gabriel, the Trustworthy and Holy Spirit, will reveal and teach the Qur'an to Muhammad, who had not known scripture or reading; this fulfills 42:52.
rows.anchor: Rûh-i Emîn, Rûhu’l-Kudüs olan Cibrîl vâsıtasıyla sana okuyacağın bir kitap olan Kur’ân’ı vahyederek indirip belleteceğiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, divine revelation will make him a possessor of the Qur'an and its recitation, including what has descended and what will descend.
rows.anchor: Yahut vahiy ile seni Kur’an ve kıraat sâhibi yapacağız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being taught to recite is a sign of divine guidance and apostleship; an exceptionally powerful memory, and the prediction and fulfillment of it, are further miracles.
rows.anchor: bu derece kuvvetli bir hıfza sâhip olmak da diğer bir âyet ve mucize olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching recitation here means teaching the Qur'an by heart, not reading it from a written page.
rows.anchor: okutmaktan murad ezbere okutmaktır. Yoksa yüzüne yazı okumak değildir

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some interpret not forgetting chiefly as acting according to the Qur'an's requirements.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da demişlerdir[^3] ki unutmamaktan asıl murad, mûcebiyle amel etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine exception preserves God's power to remove the Prophet's memory; if God made him forget permanently, that would be abrogation under 2:106.
rows.anchor: Unutturacağını tamamen unutturabilir ki bu bir nesh olur

rows.speaker: Sahîh-i Buhârî
rows.claim: In a Bukhari report, the Prophet omitted a verse while reciting in morning prayer; Ubayy thought it abrogated, asked, and the Prophet replied that he forgot.
rows.anchor: Sabah namazı idi. Übeyy onu neshedildi sanmış, sual etmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If brief forgetting occurs, God prompts the Prophet or provides a reminder, as when hearing ʿAbbād b. Bishr recite recalled verses of two suras.
rows.anchor: Abbâd b. Bişr’in[^8] kıraatini işittiğinde “Bu bana filan ve filan sûrede, şu ve şu âyeti hatırlattı”

rows.speaker: Denilmiştir
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the exception as allowing rare lapses of memory, exemplified by the prayer report.
rows.anchor: Denilmiştir ki istisnâ kıllet içindir. Nitekim Sahîh-i Buhârî’de rivayet edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Momentary omissions in prayer are neither lasting erasure nor abrogation; they can teach the community rules for inevitable lapses in recitation and prayer, or predate the promise.
rows.anchor: cüz’î bir an için vâki‘olan böyle birkaç nisyan tilâveti nesih mânasında olan müstemir insâ mâhiyetinde olmayıp

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Others treat the exception as a figurative negative: saying something occurs very rarely can mean it does not occur at all.
rows.anchor: bazıları da demişlerdir ki bu istisnâ kıllet mânasına olarak nefiyden mecazdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed verse about warriors' nicked swords exemplifies an exception that reinforces praise by seeming to introduce a fault; this rhetorical figure reinforces the negation here.
rows.anchor: kılıçlarında bazı gediklerden ibaret olması[^12] kahramanlar için bir ayıp değil, yüksek bir medihtir

rows.speaker: İsam
rows.claim: As cited by Ālūsī from the Qāḍī gloss, ʿIṣām says the exception reinforces the universal negative: the Prophet never forgets, since God will not wish him to.
rows.anchor: İsam demiştir ki: “Bu veche göre istisnâ, nefyin umumunu tekid içindir, nakz-ı umum için değildir

rows.speaker: Ferrâ
rows.claim: Farrāʾ likewise says God mentions His ability to make the Prophet forget without intending to do so; 17:86 provides a parallel conditional warning.
rows.anchor: Ferrâ buna zâhib olmuş ve demiştir ki: ‘Bu istisnâ ile Allah teâlâ Peygamberine hiçbir şeyi unutturmayı dilememiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is comparable to the exception concerning Paradise's inhabitants in 11:107–108 and the conditional warning about association in 39:65; neither implies the feared event occurs.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’e لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ [ez-Zümer 39/65] buyurulmakla ondan elbette bir şirk vukū‘bulacağını değil

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objected to Farrāʾ's construal of the exception.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân Ferrâ’nın bu tevcîhine ilişmek istemiş[^18] ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors Farrāʾ's rhetorical interpretation, commended also by Ālūsī and ʿAbduh, and says Abū Ḥayyān missed its literary force.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî gibi Abduh da Ferrâ’nın bu tevcîhini takdirde isabet eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether the exception indicates rarity or emphasizes negation, the promised miracle is freedom from lasting forgetting; a few purposeful brief lapses do not contradict it.
rows.anchor: nisyân-ı müstemir vâki‘olmamak bu vaad mûcebince Peygamber’in mu‘cizâtından birisidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception stresses that the Prophet's unfailing memory depends wholly on God's grace, not his own power.
rows.anchor: onun unutmaması kendi kuvvetinden değil, mahza Allah’ın fazl u ihsânından olduğuna tenbih içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the promise and divine will to the all embracing name Allah evokes awe, locates the matter in divinity encompassing all attributes, and clarifies 'the Highest Lord.'
rows.anchor: bu vaad ve meşiyyetin bütün esmâyı câmi‘olan Allah ism-i celîline isnad ile beyânı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening wāw marks an oath; ʿādiyāt is the feminine sound plural active participle of ʿadw, swift running, and can denote horses, camels, or other runners.
rows.anchor: Vâv kasemdir. “Âdiyat” hızla koşmak, seğirtmek mânasına “adv”den ism-i fâil

rows.speaker: Kāmûs sâhibi
rows.claim: The Kāmūs author in Basāʾir derives ʿadw from crossing a boundary: physically running, inward enmity, unjust transgression, or spatial contagion.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs sâhibinin Besâir’de beyânına göre bu “adv” maddesi esasen tecavüz mânasına mevzû‘dur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdī and ʿādiya can denote a company rushing continually into combat.
rows.anchor: dâima harb u kıtâle koşup hücum eden cemaate denir

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some restrict ʿadī to attacking infantry and ʿādiya to attacking cavalry.
rows.anchor: Bazıları “adî” piyade muhâcimlerine, “âdiye” süvari muhâcimlerine mahsus olduğunu söylemiştir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī identifies the runners as pilgrims' camels heading to ʿArafāt.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den mervî olarak Arafat’a giden huccâcın develeriyle tefsîrine dâir bir rivayet

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies them as cavalry horses; most exegetes chose this reading.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervî olduğu üzere süvarilerin atları olmak âyetlerin mazmûnuna nazaran zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context favors cavalry horses over pilgrims' camels, especially because ḍabḥ describes a horse's rapid panting, distinct from neighing and soft humming.
rows.anchor: Dabh” atların koşu esnasındaki nefeslerinin sesleridir ki “sahîl”[^4] denilen[^5] kişnemek değil

rows.speaker: Denilmiştir
rows.claim: One account says ḍabḥ occurs when a horse or dog runs.
rows.anchor: Denilmiştir ki “dabh” bir at, bir de köpek koşarken olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative ḍabḥan implies a phrase like 'they pant a panting,' or an adjective meaning 'panting ones.'
rows.anchor: Takdîr-i kelâm تضبح ضبحا veya “dâbihât” mânasındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most direct sense of 'striking fire' is horses' hooves throwing sparks from stones; the visible night sparks imply speed, strength, and a nocturnal raid.
rows.anchor: atların koşarlarken hızlarından tırnaklarıyla çarptıkları taşlardan çakmak gibi ateşler çakarak gitmelerinde zâhirdir

rows.speaker: Bir kısım müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some exegetes still understand horses but take their kindling fire as stirring up war between riders and enemies; 5:64 uses the same fire metaphor.
rows.anchor: Bir kısım müfessirîn demişlerdir ki: Gerçi bu âyetlerden murad atlardır. Lâkin ateş çakmaları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying 'the oven grew hot' likewise describes war intensifying.
rows.anchor: harb kızıştığı zaman حَمِيَ الْوَطِيسُ “fırın kızıştı” denilmek de meseldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes the fire kindlers raiders lighting night fires for needs and food; under the camel reading they are pilgrims lighting fires after reaching Muzdalifa from ʿArafāt.
rows.anchor: Bunlar geceleyin hâcetleri ve yemekleri için ateş yakan gāzilerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the fire kindlers tongues whose forceful words ignite enmity.
rows.anchor: Ağır, müheyyic sözler söyleyerek adâvet ateşi çakıp tutuşturan diller denilmiş

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for interpreting the sparks as thoughts generating cunning and deception; an idiom about striking a flint conveys devising harm or war.
rows.anchor: Mekr ü hud‘a ateşi çakan fikirlerdir denilmiş, bu mâna da İbn Abbas’tan rivayet edilmiştir

rows.speaker: İkrime
rows.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the fire striking things as spears or weapons.
rows.anchor: İkrime demiştir ki: فَٱلْمُورِيَٰتِ قَدْحًۭا süngüler, silahlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern firearms and fast motorized attack vehicles can fall under the literal wording; if the sura is Meccan, the verses anticipate future military means unavailable to early Muslims.
rows.anchor: yalnız atlara değil, harıl harıl hızlı sür‘atlerle hücum eden motorlu akın vâsıtalarının dahi hepsine şâmil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words' dense nuances resist full translation, and the successive fāʾ conjunctions can suggest progressively developing means of attack across eras.
rows.anchor: bunların aralarında [6018] peyderpey tertip ifade eden fâ’larla îrad olundukları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final interpretation takes 'striking fire' as succeeding in one's purpose, whether raid or pilgrimage, describing a successful company or the horses' riders.
rows.anchor: maksudlarını[^14] bulmuş, gazâ veya hac her ne ise matlublarına muvaffak olmuş olanlar diye tefsir edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom 'his flint struck fire' means achieving one's aim; the author cites Jarīr's verse about the Azd striking flint and a parallel saying about a generous man's success.
rows.anchor: Bu mânada Cerîr: وَجَدْنَا الأَْزْدَ أَكْرَمَهُمْ جَوَادَا وَأَوْرَاهُمْ إِذَا قَدَحُوا زِنَادَا demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoof spark sense is most apparent as literal while the other traditional senses are figurative; the literal applicability to modern weapons remains possible.
rows.anchor: Bu mânalardan birincisi doğrudan doğru hakikat, diğerleri mecaz olmak hasebiyle en zâhir olan evvelkidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early in revelation, the Prophet tried to repeat Gabriel's recitation before it ended, fearing he might miss a letter or word; this occasion connects to 75:16–19.
rows.anchor: Cebrâil vahyi henüz tamamlamadan tekrar etmeye çalışıyordu. Bu sebeple Resûlullah’a Kur’an okurken acele etmemesini emreden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction and promise stopped his haste and assured preservation of revelation; his protection from forgetting is a miracle of God's power, reflected in the community's continuing memorization.
rows.anchor: diğer taraftan da vahyin korunmasının güvenceye alındığı bildiriliyordu

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the exception signals abrogation: God makes the Prophet forget a ruling when He withdraws it.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bu istisnanın neshe delâlet ettiğini yani “Allah herhangi bir hükmü yürürlükten kaldırmak istediği zaman onu peygambere unutturur”

rows.speaker: Bazı âlimlere
rows.claim: Others say God never willed the Prophet to forget, so he never did; they compare the conditional removal of revelation in 17:86 and the exception in 11:107–108.
rows.anchor: Bazı âlimlere göre ise bu âyet –tıpkı “Gerçek şu ki, biz dilersek sana vahyettiğimizi ortadan kaldırırız”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The authors instead see a general principle of divine will, as in 76:30: God gives creatures their faculties, and the Prophet will never forget the Qur'an because God wills that outcome.
rows.anchor: Bize göre “Sizler ancak rabbinizin (bunu) dilemesi sayesinde dileyebilirsiniz” (İnsan 76/30) âyetinde olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: Exegetes take the promised ease as specific to the Prophet: God enables effortless memorization, observance of religious duties, and deeds leading to Paradise; Zamakhsharī and Rāzī are cited.
rows.anchor: Müfessirler, “Sana kolaylık ve huzurun yollarını açacağız” meâlindeki 8. âyeti de Hz. Peygamber’in şahsına özgü

rows.speaker: Şevkânî
rows.claim: Shawkānī interprets the ease as success in whichever affairs of religion or worldly life the Prophet pursues.
rows.anchor: Şevkânî ise “din ve dünya işlerinden hangisine yönelirse o yolda muvaffak kılması” anlamında yorumlamıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage depicts horses charging an enemy in battle, and swears by horses because they were among the most important elements of old warfare after humans.
rows.anchor: Savaş sırasında düşman üzerine saldıran atlar tasvir edilmekte ve eski savaşların insandan sonra en önemli unsuru olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath points to God as giver of these useful, cherished animals and draws attention to the truth and importance of the message in following verses.
rows.anchor: atları onlara bağışlayanın Allah olduğuna işaret etmek, o günün insanının gözünde çok değerli olan bu varlıklar üzerine yemin ederek

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet began reciting Gabriel's revelation before Gabriel finished for fear of forgetting; the verse was revealed in response. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it, and its chain contains the very weak Juwaybir.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه جبريل بالوحي لم يفرغ جبريل من الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's chain contains Juwaybir, whom the author rates very weak.
rows.anchor: في إسناده جويبر ضعيف جدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet sent out horses and received no news for a month, whereupon the verse was revealed; al-Bazzār, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Ḥākim transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيلا ولبث شهرا لا يأتيه منها خبر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says the Prophet dispatched a detachment against a Kināna clan under al-Mundhir b. ʿAmr al-Anṣārī; news was delayed, hypocrites claimed all were killed, and God revealed the verse about its horses.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: بعث رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سرية إلى حي من كنانة واستعمل عليهم المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet sent horses on a prolonged expedition, heard nothing for a month, and the verse was revealed; their panting came through their nostrils.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعث خيلا فأسهبت شهرا لم يأته منها خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ashabat means going far through suhūb, broad open lands; sahb is the singular.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أسهبت: أمعنت في السهوب: وهي الأرض الواسعة جمع سهب
